Best,
Asha

Operational note on inventory and provenance: we can generate a dataset origin inventory for customer projects using our ingestion pipeline metadata.

Karthik — please flag any technical limits on producing per‑model provenance exports if a customer requests them as part of contract obligations.

Subject: Re: Training-data OSS attribution & indemnity — quick context

Asha / Mina —

Thanks for the context. I attached a short proposed redline (proposed-redline-msa.pdf) that tries to balance Deep Orchard's procurement asks with Redwood's operational realities. High points:

- Narrowed indemnity trigger: Redwood will indemnify claims to the extent they arise from Redwood's grossly negligent ingestion of known proprietary content, but not for (i) customer‑supplied data, (ii) claims traceable solely to third‑party model outputs without demonstrable linkage to a dataset row we ingested.
- Evidence matrix: claimant must provide (1) notice with time/date and sample output, (2) ingestion CSV matching sample hash within 30 days, (3) Redwood engineer attestation confirming the mapping (template included).
- Cap & escape: we propose a carveout that routes low‑value claims (below $25k) to an internal remediation bucket and require insurance/escrow for claims above $250k before unlimited defense obligations kick in. This is intended to keep our exposure predictable while giving procurement comfort.
- Training provenance start date: any models trained before 2026‑10 are out of scope for provenance guarantees; we will assist with best‑effort review.

Marissa — commercial: the redline asks for a modest platform credit if Redwood must produce deep forensic exports (to offset infra time). If customer accepts a 60‑day triage period plus the evidence requirements above, I think we can avoid higher caps or deeper indemnity. Please advise on whether that credit is acceptable against DEAL‑9841 economics.

If Deep Orchard wants counsel call, we can set up a 30m with Alpha Legal + our external counsel next week.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
